She wears the Umbril opal necklace, which belonged to Eldreth's mother. While wearing the necklace, her Charisma score becomes 22, her Charisma bonus is +6, and her spell save is DC 18.

npcs.name: Elmyra Lamorieth

features.name: Spellbook
features.description: Elmyra has all the spells in her spellbook that a mage normally does, but also has the spells identify and dimension door.

npcs.description: Elmyra Lamorieth is a brilliant mage and the last living member of the Lamorieth bloodline. Her family once held great status and power in the shadow fey courts, until one of her ancestors was accused of plotting against the Queen of Night and Magic. The Lamorieth family lost all favor and were stripped of their lands and titles from that moment on. Elmyra seethes with hatred for those who cast her family into disgrace and has spent her long life mastering the arcane arts and accumulating allies outside the courts in hopes of one day restoring her family's name.

traps.name: Falling Net Trap
traps.trigger: A trip wire stretched between the trees is triggered.

detection.detail: Spotting the trip wire stretched between the trees requires a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: The trap can be disarmed (no specific DC or method given in the source).

traps.effect: A net falls from the branches, trapping those beneath it. If a PC is caught in the net, Tertso comes down to cut them free.
traps.area: Set in the branches on either side of the tree Tertso is hiding in.
traps.description: Two falling net traps are set in the branches on either side of the tree Tertso is hiding in, triggered by a trip wire stretched between the trees.

traps.name: Bramble Wall
traps.trigger: Attempting to move through the initial wall of brambles without clearing it.

detection.detail: The brambles are obvious.

disarm.method: Cut through, burn away, or otherwise clear
disarm.detail: The initial wall of brambles cannot be bypassed and must be cut through, burned away, or otherwise cleared to avoid damage (AC 8, 20 hp).

traps.effect: Moving faster than half speed on the path requires a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Animal Handling) check if mounted (or a DC 10 Dexterity [Acrobatics] check if on foot) to avoid taking 5 (2d4) points of slashing damage to their mount or themselves. After five checks, regardless of success or failure, the PCs are able to get clear of the brambles.
traps.area: The entire trail lined by thick patches of brambles.
traps.description: Dark, ominous brambles have encroached on this trailhead, and rows of thorns glisten in the hazy twilight all along the edges of the forked path that follows.

traps.name: Poisoned Dart Trip Wire
traps.trigger: Opening the door cuts a trip wire that unleashes four poisoned darts.

detection.detail: A successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check notices the trip wire through a gap in the door.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 13 Dexterity check using thieves' tools cuts the trip wire harmlessly. A PC without thieves' tools can attempt this check with disadvantage using an edged weapon or tool. On a failure, the wire hasn't been cut sufficiently, permitting the trap to trigger when the door is opened.

traps.effect: Make a ranged weapon attack for each dart with a +7 bonus to hit, selecting random targets outside that are within 10 feet of the door. A creature that is hit takes 3 (1d6) piercing damage and must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw, taking 7 (2d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Once triggered, the darts and tripwire must be reset to allow the trap to function once more.
traps.area: Targets outside within 10 feet of the door
traps.description: A trip wire connected to four poisoned darts is set to fire when the locked door of the goblin leader's abode is opened.

traps.name: Sarastra's Holy Book
traps.trigger: Opening the book

detection.detail: Not specified

disarm.detail: Not specified

traps.effect: Any creature other than Hypatia who opens her copy of the book must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be blinded for 1 hour.
traps.description: An ancient-looking copy of Sarastra's holy book, Mistress of Air and Darkness, sits on the table in Hypatia's room. Any creature other than Hypatia who opens it must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be blinded for 1 hour.

traps.name: Dark Script
traps.trigger: A PC lights the lantern in area 2.

detection.detail: Any PC with the ability to cast 1st-level sorcerer or wizard spells automatically discerns the dangerous nature of the writing. If a PC can read the writing through magical means, they learn the writing's trap triggers if the lantern is lit, though what the nature of the trap is remains a mystery.

disarm.detail: The trap functions as an 8th-level spell and can be dispelled using dispel magic.

traps.effect: A PC who lights the lantern immediately suffers the effects of the maze spell for 10 minutes or until they escape.
traps.description: The writing on the wall is a powerful spell trap written in a forgotten language known as Old Umbral.

traps.name: Magical Fence
traps.trigger: Attempting to cross into the courtyard while the fence is active

detection.detail: Spidery runes engraved on the posts flicker with a bluish glow. A weave of transparent, bluish energy stretches between the posts, blocking access to the courtyard beyond. As the runes flicker and dim, the weave of energy flickers in and out of existence with a faint humming noise.

disarm.detail: If one of the posts is destroyed, any sections of fence it connects to cease to function altogether. Each post has AC 17 and 18 hp and a damage threshold of 10.

traps.effect: During the periods it stands, it functions as a wall of force, except it is translucent (rather than entirely transparent), and there are strategically-placed gaps in the wall through which defenders could make ranged attacks. Any creature standing adjacent to the fence has three-quarters cover against attacks at a range of 10 feet or more from the other side. If the PCs attempt to cross into the courtyard, they must rush through while one of the sections of the fence is down. A successful DC 13 Dexterity saving throw allows safe passage past the fence. On a failed save, a creature takes 22 (4d10) points of force damage and is thrown back 5 feet and falls prone. However, any damage dealt to a post that does not reduce it to 0 hp releases a surge of energy. All creatures within 5 feet of a post when it surges take 11 (2d10) points of force damage. A successful DC 13 Dexterity saving throw reduces the damage by half.
traps.area: The fence stretches between the posts blocking access to the courtyard beyond.
traps.description: This magical fence once provided the primary means of defense for the palace. Decades of neglect have caused the magic to malfunction; as a result, the fence now flickers in and out of existence at random intervals.

traps.name: Glyph of Warding (Trapdoor)
traps.trigger: Opening the trapdoor without saying the phrase, "Wine for m'lady"

detection.detail: The glyph can be discovered with a DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana or Investigation) check.

traps.effect: A blast of magical energy in a 20-foot radius, forcing each creature in the area to make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 22 (5d8) fire damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.description: The trapdoor leading to the cellar has a glyph of warding cast on it. Opening the door without saying the phrase, "Wine for m'lady" causes a blast of magical energy in a 20-foot radius.

traps.name: Trapped Final Step
traps.trigger: If more than 10 pounds are placed on the step

detection.detail: A successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check reveals the final step is trapped.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 12 Intelligence (Arcana) check also reveals the trap can be disabled by poking the open eye of the winking figure in the painting.

traps.effect: The figure in the painting opens its mouth and releases a blast of frigid cold. Each creature within 5 feet of the final step must make a successful DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 16 (3d10) damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: Each creature within 5 feet of the final step
traps.description: A trapped final step that releases a blast of frigid cold from a painting when more than 10 pounds are placed on it.

traps.name: Enhanced Glyph of Warding
traps.trigger: Destroying the door, or a failed check to disable the glyph

detection.detail: Any active glyphs on the doors can be found with a successful DC 25 Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 20 Intelligence (Arcana) check can be used to disable a glyph.

traps.effect: The glyph explodes in a 20-foot radius; creatures in the area of effect must succeed on a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw or take 27 (6d8) cold damage, or half that much damage on a successful one.
traps.description: Doors in the labyrinth are locked and trapped with an enhanced glyph of warding; following the path from the center of the labyrinth to a door unlocks the door and disables the trap.

traps.name: Time Trap (Beneath and Under Door)
traps.trigger: Passing through the door

detection.detail: The door is unlocked and appears normal; the clock face reads 3:16 and the doormat reads 6.

disarm.detail: To bypass the effect, the clock's hands must be arranged so that if one were to subtract all of the individual digits from each other, going from left to right (for example 9 – 2 – 1), the result would be 6.

traps.effect: The door alters time, and those passing through it are subjected to a random temporal effect (see the "Temporal Effects" sidebar).
traps.description: A wooden door with a clock face mounted on it hangs in an archway that faces the steps. The clock reads, "3:16." The door is closed. The doormat reads, "6." The door alters time for those passing through it.

traps.name: Hammerbell Alarms
traps.trigger: Stepping onto the staircase without first opening the Beneath and Under Door

detection.detail: The clocks with hammer bell alarms are visible throughout the tower.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified; avoid by opening the door first.

traps.effect: All the clocks with hammer bell alarms go off simultaneously. All creatures in the tower (except The Ticktock Man) must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or lose any concentration spells and become deafened for 1 minute, or if successful, until the start of their next turn.
traps.area: All creatures in the tower (except The Ticktock Man)
traps.description: All hammer bell alarm clocks in the tower go off at once, deafening and disrupting concentration.

traps.name: Time Trap (Up and Over Door)
traps.trigger: Passing through the door

detection.detail: The door is unlocked and appears normal; the clock face reads 7:29 and the doormat reads 9.

disarm.detail: To bypass the effect, the clock's hands must be arranged so that if one were to add all the individual digits together (for example 3 + 3 + 3), the result would be 9.

traps.effect: The door alters time, and those passing through it are subjected to a random temporal effect (see the "Temporal Effects" sidebar).
traps.description: A wooden plank door with a clock face mounted on it hangs in an archway that stands directly at the top of the steps. "7:29." The door is closed. The doormat reads, "9." The door alters time for those passing through it.

traps.name: Cuckoo Alarms
traps.trigger: Triggered in conjunction with the Up and Over Door area (specific trigger not fully detailed in this text)

detection.detail: The cuckoo clocks are visible throughout the tower.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

traps.effect: All the cuckoo clocks in the tower ring simultaneously. The cacophony is maddening, and all creatures in the tower (except The Ticktock Man) must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw to avoid losing concentration on any active spells.
traps.area: All creatures in the tower (except The Ticktock Man)
traps.description: All cuckoo clocks ring at once, creating a maddening cacophony that disrupts concentration.

traps.name: Enchanted Door Memory Siphon
traps.trigger: Passing through the door

detection.detail: No detection method specified

disarm.detail: To bypass the effect, the clock's hands must be arranged so that if one were to multiply the individual digits together, going from left to right (for example 2 × 3 × 2), the result would be 12.

traps.effect: Those passing through it must make a DC 16 Wisdom save or lose their background, including proficiency in any skills, tools, and languages associated with the background. The memories transform into colored sand and manifest within one of the hourglasses atop the shelf in the Nowhere Room. The effect lasts until the individual recovers their memories, as described below.
traps.description: The enchanted door siphons memories.

traps.name: Hungry Demon Puzzle Lock
traps.trigger: Placing items that don't contain the specified colors (blue, yellow, purple) into the balor's mouth, or offering a name other than a member of the Kairious family when asked.

detection.detail: The hollow inside the demon's mouth is pitch black. If a light is shone inside it, the following words can be seen engraved in a tiny, neat script: I relish cobalt, dote on flax, and periwinkle my diet lacks.

disarm.detail: The northern door is locked and cannot be opened with a physical key or thieves' tools. The puzzle must be solved by placing a blue, yellow, and purple object of any material (multicolored items can be used if one or more of the listed colors is present on it) in the balor's mouth, or by casting a spell that produces an array of colors, such as color spray or prismatic spray into it. Then, when asked 'Who are you?', a PC must offer the name of a member of the Kairious family.

traps.effect: If the wrong items or name are given, the demon's face makes a disgusted expression and wakes the gorgons disguised as the steel bull statues. The gorgons cannot easily escape the room and fight to the death.
traps.description: A locked door with a carved balor's head that opens only when the correct colored items are placed in its mouth and a Kairious family name is given.

traps.name: Time Trap
traps.trigger: Each time a creature steps on one of the tiles in the courtyard.

detection.detail: The tiles' appearance changes with age: pristine in the first 25 feet, scuffed with slight patina in the second 25 feet, heavily worn with hairline fractures in the third 25 feet, and chipped with wide cracks and broken edges in the fourth 25 feet.

disarm.detail: A creature can escape the aging effects by traversing the courtyard in the following fashion: (1) slithering, then (2) crawling, then (3) dancing, then (4) stooping and walking with a cane.

traps.effect: Each time a creature steps on one of the tiles, they age a certain amount depending on where in the courtyard they are. Refer to the "Time Trap Aging" table to determine how much aging occurs with each step, how one can avoid the aging effect, and what the tiles in each section look like. A creature that enters the courtyard from anywhere other than the stairs ages 100 years for its first step, then the trap functions as described above. A creature standing within the vapor emitted by the shroud of Kairious is immune to the effects of the trap.
traps.area: The courtyard is laid in orderly five-foot squares of white onyx; they start out pristine, as if freshly laid, then progressively show more and more signs of age the closer one gets to the vault door. Directly in front of the double doors, there is a slightly raised long dais made of smooth, polished stone that spans 30 feet long by 5 feet wide.
traps.description: A magical trap in a courtyard that ages creatures as they step on tiles, with the aging effect increasing closer to the vault door.

traps.name: Explosive Glyph
traps.trigger: Hidden within the locking mechanism of the padlock; triggered when the lock is broken or when the glyph's trigger condition is met.

detection.detail: A magical glyph is hidden within the locking mechanism of the padlock.

disarm.detail: The padlock can be picked with a successful DC 16 Dexterity check using thieves' tools. A success also disables the effect of the glyph of warding.

traps.effect: Its explosive runes erupt with magical energy as described in the spell glyph of warding. The spell was cast at 3rd level and is set to deal fire damage.
traps.description: A magical glyph hidden within the locking mechanism of the padlock on the iron gate. If triggered, its explosive runes erupt with magical energy as described in the spell glyph of warding, cast at 3rd level and set to deal fire damage.

traps.name: Putrid Bog Stench
traps.trigger: Any non-resident of the bog entering the Putrid Bog

detection.detail: The putrid stench is immediately obvious; no check required to notice.

disarm.detail: Cannot be disarmed; a protection from poison spell removes the effect from a sickened creature and renders them immune to the effects for the remainder of the visit.

traps.effect: Any non-resident of the bog must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or gain the poisoned condition from the bog's putrid stench for as long as they remain within its confines. A successful save renders them immune to the effects of the bog's stench for the duration of the visit. A protection from poison spell removes the effect from a sickened creature and renders them immune to the effects for the remainder of the visit. Creatures with immunity to poison are unaffected, and creatures with poison resistance receive their normal advantage on the saving throws.
traps.description: The Putrid Bog is covered in dank brackish water and thick mud. Any non-resident must save or be poisoned by the bog's putrid stench.
traps.source: Shadows of the Dusk Queen p.167

traps.name: Symbol of Stunning (Black Rock Altar)
traps.trigger: Anyone not of evil alignment passing through the ring of standing stones

detection.detail: The black rock altar radiates a permanent symbol of stunning; a palpable feeling of evil and dark magic radiates from the entire area and the black altar in particular.

disarm.detail: Not specified.

traps.effect: The black rock altar radiates a permanent symbol of stunning (successful DC 16 Wisdom saving throw negates), which is triggered by anyone not of evil alignment passing through the ring of standing stones.
traps.area: Ring of standing stones, approximately 30 feet in diameter
traps.description: A permanent symbol of stunning on the black rock altar at the heart of the Putrid Bog triggers when a non-evil creature passes through the ring of standing stones.
traps.source: Shadows of the Dusk Queen p.167

traps.name: Shard of the Mirror
traps.trigger: Disturbing or attempting to remove the shard from the tree

detection.detail: The shard is visible; failing either of these checks by 3 or more requires a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw to avoid being cut by the shard for 3 (1d6) slashing damage. Failing either check by 10 or more requires a successful DC 17 Dexterity saving throw to avoid falling from the tree for 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage.

disarm.detail: The shard is too firmly embedded in the tree for mage hand or similar magic to pull free.

traps.effect: Being cut by the shard for 3 (1d6) slashing damage, or falling from the tree for 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage.
traps.description: A shard embedded in a tree that cuts those who fail to remove it carefully, with a risk of falling.

traps.name: Pit of Shadows Steps
traps.trigger: Attempting to navigate the steep and uneven steps

detection.detail: A DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check reveals a partially worn and eroded set of ancient stone steps cut into the sides of the pit.

disarm.detail: If the PCs take precautionary measures, such as using rope or other climbing gear, the checks are made with advantage.

traps.effect: PCs failing a DC 12 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check fall from the steps and crash to the stone ledge below, taking 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage.
traps.area: The steps leading down into the pit
traps.description: Extremely steep and uneven steps that are difficult to navigate, causing falls.

traps.name: Glyph of Warding on Tower Door
traps.trigger: Opening or touching the warded door

detection.detail: The door is warded with arcane lock and protected by a glyph of warding.

disarm.detail: Not specified.

traps.effect: 31 (7d8) cold damage, DC 18 Dexterity saving throw for half.
traps.description: A glyph of warding protecting the tower's front door.

traps.name: Bramble Path
traps.trigger: Moving faster than half speed on the path

detection.detail: The brambles are obvious and visible

disarm.detail: Cannot be disarmed; must be avoided by moving at half speed or making checks

traps.effect: Moving faster than half speed on the path requires a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Animal Handling) check if mounted (or a DC 10 Dexterity [Acrobatics] check if on foot) to avoid taking 5 (2d4) points of slashing damage to their mount or themselves. After five checks, regardless of success or failure, the PCs are able to get clear of the brambles.
traps.area: Entire trail lined by thick patches of brambles
traps.description: This entire trail is lined by thick patches of brambles that are difficult to avoid.

traps.name: Frigid Blast Step Trap
traps.trigger: If more than 10 pounds are placed on the final step

detection.detail: A successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check reveals the final step is trapped.

traps.effect: The figure in the painting opens its mouth and releases a blast of frigid
traps.description: The final step of the stairwell is trapped; when more than 10 pounds are placed on it, the figure in the painting opens its mouth and releases a blast of frigid (text truncated).
traps.source: The Sodality of Silent Rites p.103

traps.name: Glyph of Warding (Front Door)
traps.trigger: Opening or entering the warded door

detection.detail: The door is warded with arcane lock and protected by a glyph of warding.

traps.effect: 31 (7d8) cold damage, DC 18 Dexterity saving throw for half.
traps.area: The front door of the Dusk Queen's Tower
traps.description: A glyph of warding protecting the front door of the tower.
